extracted.intended_audience: Faculty investigators preparing an NIH NIAID Academic Research Enhancement Award (R15/PA-16-200) application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and example content for preparing and formatting an NIH Academic Research Enhancement Award (R15, FOA PA-16-200) application, including required SF424 fields, Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment inventories, biosketches, letters of support, and resource authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA-specific application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Summary/Abstract must succinctly state the proposed activities, significance, goals, and specific aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example elements: high-impact objective to develop new inhibitors; background on ricin and Shiga toxin; description of proposed approach (use of VPg), enumerated goals (e.g., establish conditions for complex formation; determine minimal inhibitory peptide; optimize inhibition conditions); statement of innovation and expected outcomes (therapeutic leads, structural/mechanistic rationale); note on student training and capacity building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Public Health Relevance Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Narrative that states the public health relevance of the research and ties it to the Institute's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Explain how ricin and related toxins are lethal, lack effective treatments, pose bioterrorism and public health threats, and how the proposed work addresses these concerns and aligns with NIAID's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 and administrative completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SF-424 (R&R) cover page and all required administrative fields (applicant information, DUNS/EIN, type of submission, dates, authorized representative, signatures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organizational DUNS, legal name, department, contact PD/PI info, employer identification number, type of applicant, whether application is a New/Resubmission/Renewal/Revision, federal identifier fields, and signature/certification agreeing to statements and assurances. Accurately mark 'Is this application being submitted to other agencies?' and other routing fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctly indicate application type and resubmission details
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark the appropriate box for 'TYPE OF APPLICATION' (New, Resubmission, Renewal, Continuation, Revision) and if a resubmission, indicate the nature of changes (e.g., A. Increase Award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to correctly indicate submission type is an administrative deficiency; include prior grants.gov tracking numbers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, vertebrate animals, and related compliance declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state whether human subjects or vertebrate animals are involved and provide necessary regulatory details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects: declare exemption status or pending IRB, provide IRB approval date and assurance number. If vertebrate animals: indicate IACUC review status and approval date and animal welfare assurance number. Also declare if proprietary information is included, environmental impact, historic site status, and international activities, with explanations as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: institutional characteristics and assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional characteristics (e.g., minority-serving status, undergraduate/graduate enrollment) and the resources available to support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include student demographics, campus facilities, library access, computing services, wireless/hardwired networks, office/lab locations, and statement of institutional commitment to research and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: laboratory and core resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed description of laboratory spaces, safety infrastructure, and shared instrumentation available to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List biosafety cabinets, fume hoods, autoclaves, water purification, microscopy suites, NMR facility, cell culture facilities, -80C freezers, ultracentrifuge, ICP-MS, and other core instruments; indicate proximity to PI lab and availability for research use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: student research programs and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional student research programs, mentoring structures, and opportunities for undergraduate/graduate training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe programs (e.g., PRISM), number of students supported, training courses, travel support for conferences, symposiums, mentoring relationships, evidence of student success (presentations, publications), and links to broader diversity/inclusion efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: institutional collaborations and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe formal and informal collaborations with other institutions and their contributions to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List community college partnerships, doctoral program affiliations, collaborations with research institutions (e.g., Columbia, Mount Sinai), international consortia, and specific contributions such as access to facilities or expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for early-stage investigators and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail institutional mechanisms to support early-stage investigators (start-up packages, course release policies, Office for Advancement of Research programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mention of dean/Chancellor support, internal funding programs (emergency funds, pilot money, proposal peer review, open-access funding), and other incentives that demonstrate institutional commitment to faculty research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment inventory and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive inventory of major equipment available to the project, both shared and PI-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include major instruments (GC/MS, HPLC, LC-MS, real-time PCR, genetic analyzers, microplate readers, NMR, microscopy, cell culture equipment), teaching/research dual-use instruments, and PI's lab-specific instruments (e.g., AKTA pure, fluorometer, HPLC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch format and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare NIH-format biographical sketches for senior/key personnel that conform to page limits and required sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biosketch instructions: DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES. Include name, eRA Commons user name, position title, education/training table, A. Personal Statement (relevance to proposed research), B. Positions and Honors, and C. Contributions to Science with selected publications. Attach Current & Pending Support as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support: collaborator commitments and resource descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain letters from collaborators and institutional officials that state the nature of support, resources to be provided, and endorsement of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify offered resources (laboratory space, reagents, instrumentation), roles in the project (e.g., perform isothermal calorimetry, crystallography), and explicit endorsement of applicant's capacity to complete the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate key biological resources and provide vendor/catalog information per NIH policy to enhance reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List key resources (cell lines, strains), provide commercial source (vendor), catalog numbers, and note that purchased cell lines 'come with the company’s authentication certificate.' State that authentication will be performed as appropriate and according to NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and training compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Document biosafety measures, hazardous-waste and biohazard training, and other compliance training for personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List availability of biosafety cabinets, fume hoods, annual mandatory seminars on Hazardous Waste Disposal, seminars on Biohazardous Substances/Radioactivity, and confirmation that key personnel have completed RCR and COI training. If work involves radioactivity or dangerous toxins, state where such experiments will be performed and whether licenses are pending/held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement on proprietary information, environmental and historic impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare inclusion of proprietary/privileged information, potential environmental impacts, and whether the research site is or could be a historic place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No boxes and provide explanations when 'Yes' is chosen; address environmental assessment (EA/EIS) status if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and FOIA / confidentiality notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide notices about accessibility (Section 508) and FOIA redaction policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact for accessibility issues and note that FOIA responses may include substantial redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments/deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and bibliography attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a bibliography & references cited file as part of the Research Plan materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comprehensive list of citations supporting background, methodology, and precedence for proposed approaches; include methods references for assays and instrumentation where relevant.
